description.content:
**Test Credentials**
| Merchant Till | Secret Key | Status |
|----------------|------------|--------|
| 133238 | hyqd7bwMr9Kv-C5PW4n7uF4TiMnMp_hyvyhYYkYlcU8 | Active |
| 133239 | hyqd7bwMr9Kv-C5PW4n7uF4TiMnMp_hyvyhYYkYlcU8 | Active |
| 133240 | hyqd7bwMr9Kv-C5PW4n7uF4TiMnMp_hyvyhYYkYlcU8 | Active |
**Integration steps**

**Step 1 — Get authorization.**

 Obtain an OAuth2 bearer token with your
API credentials and send it as `Authorization: Bearer {access_token}`
on every call. Obtain a fresh token before it expires — a request
with an expired token is rejected. Content-Type must be
`application/json`.

**Step 2 — Sign the payload.**

 Build the canonical string
`merchantTill|timestamp|nonce` (pipe-joined, no whitespace, no
trailing separator) and compute the lowercase-hex HMAC-SHA256
digest of it, keyed with the till's secret. Generate `timestamp`
and `nonce` fresh for every request, including retries — reusing a
nonce inside the replay window is rejected even on a retry of the
same txnReference. The signature covers only merchantTill,
timestamp and nonce — not the amount, recipient or channel;
integrity of the rest of the payload comes from TLS, so send over
https only.

    import hmac, hashlib, uuid
    from datetime import datetime, timezone

    # Sandbox secret for till 133239 — use your own outside sandbox
    SECRET_KEY = "hyqd7bwMr9Kv-C5PW4n7uF4TiMnMp_hyvyhYYkYlcU8"
    MERCHANT_TILL = "133239"

    timestamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    nonce = str(uuid.uuid4()).lower()

    message = f"{MERCHANT_TILL}|{timestamp}|{nonce}"
    signature = hmac.new(
        SECRET_KEY.encode("utf-8"),
        message.encode("utf-8"),
        hashlib.sha256
    ).hexdigest()  # lowercase hex — not Base64

Verify your implementation against this worked example before
sending a live request — same inputs must reproduce the same
signature: secret key
`hyqd7bwMr9Kv-C5PW4n7uF4TiMnMp_hyvyhYYkYlcU8`, merchantTill
`133239`, timestamp `2026-07-21T08:47:12Z`, nonce
`c2a91b7e-4d05-4f8a-a3c6-9e1f5d7b2a48` -> signature
`8b48798149f4f71095dabbeea88c116730fb56f18c90970b39d992442f9561c9`.
Sandbox accepts only tills 133238, 133239 and 133240, all sharing
this secret key — any other till is rejected with statusCode 401
before a signature is even evaluated, since an unregistered till
has no secret key to verify against. Repeated invalid signatures
trigger a temporary lockout during which even a correct request
fails — verify against the worked example rather than by trial and
error.

**Step 3 — Build the request body.**

 Assemble the service envelope
(`serviceCode`, `txnReference`, `requestParameters`) with the
signed `timestamp`, `nonce` and `signature` nested inside
`requestParameters` alongside `merchantTill`, `recipientMobileNo`,
`amount`, `purposeOfPayment` and `channel` (set to `MPESA`). See
ProcessSendMoneyMpesaRequest below. `recipientMobileNo` accepts
2547XXXXXXXX, 07XXXXXXXX or +2547XXXXXXXX and is validated against
the mobile money register before any money moves — the recipient
needs an active M-Pesa account, not a LOOP account. `txnReference`
must be unique across every request you have ever sent — a repeat
is refused as a duplicate, which is exactly what makes a retry
safe. A transfer fee and tax are applied on top of `amount` and
drawn from your till, so the recipient receives the full amount
you specify.

    {
      "serviceCode": "MRCHNT_SENDMONEY",
      "txnReference": "7b3d9f2a-5e8c-4a1d-9f6b-2e4c7a0d8b5f",
      "requestParameters": {
        "merchantTill": "133239",
        "recipientMobileNo": "254705568254",
        "amount": "1500.00",
        "purposeOfPayment": "Refund for order INV-2026-000123",
        "channel": "MPESA",
        "timestamp": "2026-07-21T08:47:12Z",
        "nonce": "c2a91b7e-4d05-4f8a-a3c6-9e1f5d7b2a48",
        "signature": "8b48798149f4f71095dabbeea88c116730fb56f18c90970b39d992442f9561c9"
      }
    }

**Step 4 — Send the request.**

 POST the signed body with your bearer
token to `/services/process-request`. This endpoint is
shared across LOOP's products — `serviceCode` selects Send Money,
and `channel` selects where the money lands (LOOP, MPESA or
PESALINK). If you do not receive a response, treat it as
unresolved, never as a failure — see Step 6.

**Step 5 — Read the response.**

 There is no callback on this endpoint
— the synchronous response is the complete answer. Branch on the
`statusCode` field inside the response body, not the HTTP status
line — the gateway returns HTTP 200 for almost every outcome,
handled failures included. `data.serviceTransactionStatus` is
COMPLETED once the transfer has executed;
`response.transferStatus` of `S` confirms the rail's own success
signal. Individual response fields are returned only when
available for the transaction — key your reconciliation on
`transactionRef` and `transferOrderId`, and log both together with
your own `txnReference` for every payout.

**Step 6 — Handle failures and retries.**

 Never retry a timeout with a
new txnReference — you don't know whether the transfer executed,
and a repeat with the same txnReference is safely refused as a
duplicate if it already went through, while a new reference risks
paying twice. On a 500, 502, or a timeout, retry with the *same*
txnReference and fresh timestamp/nonce/signature, using
exponential backoff. On any 4xx statusCode, correct the payload
before retrying — resending it unchanged fails the same way. A 461
(recipient validation failed) always means nothing was sent. See
the statusCode table on the 200 response below for the full set of
causes.

**Step 7 — Test in sandbox, then go live.**

 Sandbox exercises the same
validation, statusCodes and response shape as production, without
moving funds — use one of tills 133238, 133239 or 133240 with
channel MPESA and any correctly formatted mobile number. Production
tills, secrets and endpoint URL are issued per merchant at
onboarding. Payouts move real, non-reversible funds in production
— authorise them on your side before the call, since this endpoint
sends whatever it is asked to send; start with small amounts.

response.name:
The gateway returns HTTP 200 for essentially every outcome, success or handled failure — branch on the `statusCode` field inside the response body, not the HTTP status line. Checks are applied in order and fail fast — the first failure ends the request, and no money leaves your till until every check passes:

| statusCode | Meaning | Returned when | Your action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 200 | Success | The transfer was executed. | Record the references. |
| 400 | Bad request | A required field is missing/empty; amount is non-numeric or ≤ 0; recipientMobileNo fails format validation; channel is not one of LOOP, MPESA, PESALINK. | Fix the payload. |
| 401 | Unauthorized | The till is not registered to you, or the signature, timestamp or nonce did not verify. | Check the till and re-sign. |
| 404 | Duplicate reference | A request already exists for this txnReference. | If retrying, the original was already accepted — do not resend with a new reference. |
| 461 | Recipient validation failed | The mobile number could not be validated as an active M-Pesa account. Nothing was sent. | Verify the recipient's number with them and retry. |
| 462 | No payment instrument | No usable payment instrument was available for this channel and amount. | Check the till balance and the amount. |
| 463 | Merchant lookup failed | The till supplied did not resolve to a merchant. | Verify the till number. |
| 464 | Transfer declined | The transfer was declined because of the data supplied. | Read message for the reason, correct and retry. |
| 500 | System error | An unexpected error while processing. | Retry with the same txnReference; escalate if persistent. |
| 502 | Service error | The service was temporarily unable to process the request. Not caused by your payload. | Retry with the same txnReference; escalate if persistent. |
| 503 | Validation unavailable | The recipient validation service was temporarily unavailable. No money moved. | Retry after a short delay with the same txnReference. |
| 562 | Validation data error | The validation reply was missing data required to proceed. No money moved. | Escalate — this is a problem on LOOP's side, not your payload. |

A statusCode can arise from more than one check — where it appears more than once in practice, the `message` field distinguishes the cause. data is an empty object `{}` on every non-200 statusCode.

description.content: Added as a part of security scheme: oauth2

Send Money — M-Pesa channel — pay money out of your merchant till
into a recipient's M-Pesa account, in a single synchronous call. The
same underlying endpoint serves three channels (LOOP, MPESA and
PESALINK) with an identical request body; only the channel value and
the destination differ. This document covers MPESA. There is no
callback on this endpoint — by the time you receive statusCode 200,
the transfer has already been executed and the response carries its
references; a non-200 means the transfer did not happen. See the
Integration steps in the operation description below.
